title: CancerYounity: A mixed-methods evaluation of a participatory science communication intervention for nutrition and cancer prevention
summary: Cancer is a disease in which harmful cells multiply uncontrollably in the body. Many types of cancer could be prevented if people changed their lifestyle habits. Diet is particularly important in this regard.  An unhealthy diet, being overweight, and drinking alcohol can increase the risk of cancer. Young people in vocational training or university programs often decide for themselves for the first time how they eat and live. They enjoy trying new things. That is why initiatives aimed at disease prevention can be especially helpful for this age group. In our project, we are working with young people to develop simple and easy-to-understand resources on nutrition and cancer prevention. These resources will then be used in vocational schools, universities, and online. The study examines how in-person lessons and social media content influence knowledge, attitudes, and confidence in one's ability to make healthy choices.
conditions: None (Cancer prevention with a focus on nutrition)

interventions.name: Participants taking part in a co‑created in‑person science communication format (such as an action or information day, a meet‑the‑expert session, or a cooking workshop)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Trainee, student, director, or coordinator at a participating regional training center or university
- Sufficient German-language proficiency to complete the questionnaires
- Provision of informed consent
- For minors, provision of informed consent from parents or legal guardians
- Access to an internet-enabled device (e.g., smartphone, tablet, or laptop) to complete the digital questionnaires
Exclusion criteria:
Age < 18 years without informed parental/legal guardian consent
